Works with

Rugged tablet for Clik Jobs and Clik Service

Clik Service is Windows job management software from Clik Limited, a Bristol company that has written service management and certification software since 2000 and sells mainly to HVAC and refrigeration, fire and security, electrical and plumbing contractors. The office runs Clik Service on a PC or server; engineers carry Clik Jobs, the companion app for Android and iOS that links to the Clik Service database. In 2024 Clik became part of Joblogic, and Clik's own website now steers new customers to Joblogic FSM and Clik Compliance while keeping a support portal for existing Clik Service installations. This page is therefore for firms already running Clik Service who need devices for the engineers using Clik Jobs; a firm starting fresh should read our Joblogic page instead.

On site, the Google Play listing says engineers use Clik Jobs to select and modify jobs, add time, materials, equipment and documents, attach photos to job sheets, take a customer's signature when the work is complete, and create jobs on the device when one starts unexpectedly. GPS sends engineers' routes back to the office. The app is described as designed to function almost completely without an active internet connection, with a connection needed only to sync, which is exactly the pattern of a boiler room, a plant deck or a rural fire alarm panel with no signal. That is a device that lives in a van, gets handed to a customer and spends its day in dust and damp.

This page sets out what Clik publishes about the devices Clik Jobs and Clik Service run on, which Tuga devices meet those published requirements, one caution about the age of the Android app, and how a UK contractor can buy a single trial unit before equipping a team.

Requirements

What Clik Service and the Clik Jobs app needs from a device

Each item below comes from Clik Limited (Clik Software), part of Joblogic since 2024's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 5.0 or later for the Clik Jobs app

    The Google Play listing for Clik Jobs (package com.clik.clikmobile, developer CLIK LIMITED, support contact hello@cliksoftware.com) shows a minimum of Android 5.0 (API level 21) and device chips for Phone and Tablet. When checked on 25 October 2026 the current version was 1.37.2, updated 8 July 2024, with the listing first released on 16 July 2014 and more than 10,000 downloads. No RAM, storage or screen size figure is published. An app whose last update is more than two years old may not have been tested by its maker on recent Android releases, so trial it on the device you intend to buy. Source: play.google.com

  • Installed from Google Play or the App Store, paired to Clik Service with a code

    Clik's support article Downloading and Installing Clik Jobs says to open the Google Play Store for Android or the Apple App Store and search for Clik Jobs, press Continue, then, for existing customers, enter the pair code or PIN retrieved from Clik Service and log in with an account that has the correct privileges. New customers can press Demo to use a demo database. The first sync copies the Clik Service data the app needs and the article advises doing it over Wi-Fi to avoid mobile data charges. No Windows version of the app is offered. Source: cliksoftware.com

  • Offline working, with a connection to sync

    The Google Play listing says an internet connection is only required to sync jobs and that Clik Jobs has been designed to function almost completely without an active internet connection. Clik's support centre FAQ answers the question of whether engineers can access their jobs offline with yes: download the job before going out onto site and sync it back to the office when reconnected. How much data the app holds on the device is not published. Source: cliksoftware.com

  • Sync driven from Clik Service, on a schedule the office sets

    The Syncing to Clik Jobs article says the Clik Service sync updates the app with modified users and privileges, edited jobs and anything linked to them, new job information including links and images, audit logs and notifications, and also synchronises customers, addresses, equipment, contacts and products. A sync can be run from a job sheet or scheduled under Settings, Settings, Modules, Clik Jobs; the article gives every 15 minutes as an example and warns against syncing as often as every 5 minutes because it can stop engineers downloading their jobs. Source: cliksoftware.com

  • Photos, signatures, GPS routes and job creation in the app

    The Google Play listing says Clik Jobs allows you to attach photos to job sheets and take a customer's signature once your work is complete, to add time items, material items, equipment and documents to jobs, to create jobs on the device and synchronise them later, and that GPS allows the office to track engineers with routes sent back and viewable at any time. No barcode or QR scanning is described, and no camera resolution or location accuracy is specified. Source: play.google.com

  • Windows for Clik Service itself: .NET Framework 4.7.2 or higher

    Clik's article Checking Your Microsoft .Net Version states that Microsoft .NET Framework 4.7.2 or higher is required to run Clik software, including Clik Service, Clik Cert and NICEIC Cert Software, and that a PC or server running the latest Windows updates should already have it. The support centre FAQ says software specifications are on the product pages, but when checked on 25 October 2026 those pages redirect to Joblogic FSM and Clik Compliance marketing and no processor, RAM, disk or Windows version figure for Clik Service is published. Clik Service is office software for a PC or server, not a field app, and Clik Jobs has no Windows version. Source: cliksoftware.com

  • Clik is now part of Joblogic

    Joblogic's announcement, last updated 26 September 2024, says Clik has officially become part of the Joblogic family and that Joblogic is working on a cloud launch of Clik's electronic certification software. Clik's homepage now presents Joblogic FSM and Clik Compliance and offers a support portal for existing Clik Service installations. Existing users should ask Clik or Joblogic how long Clik Service and Clik Jobs will be supported before buying a fleet of devices around them. Source: joblogic.com

Setting up

Getting Clik Service and the Clik Jobs app running

  1. In Clik Service, check the engineer is set up as a user with the privileges Clik Jobs needs and retrieve the pair code or PIN, as Clik's installation article describes. Ask Clik or Joblogic support how long Clik Service and Clik Jobs will be supported if you are buying several devices.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install Clik Jobs (package com.clik.clikmobile, developer CLIK LIMITED), open it, press Continue, enter the pair code or PIN and log in.
  3. Run the first sync on Wi-Fi, as Clik advises, so the app downloads your Clik Service data without using mobile data; it can take a while on a large database.
  4. In Clik Service, under Settings, Settings, Modules, Clik Jobs, set a sync schedule (Clik's article gives every 15 minutes as an example) and tick Sync by Default for the engineer, so assigned jobs reach the device without anyone pressing a button.
  5. Complete a test job on the device without signal: add time and materials, attach a photo, take a signature, then reconnect and sync, and check the audit log in Clik Service shows the job as received.
  6. Fit the vehicle mounting dock for the A8 or A10 and keep the 12V car charger in the van; for a shared A10 that returns to the office, add the charging dock, and for an A6 the belt holster.

Questions

Clik Service and the Clik Jobs app on a Tuga device

Clik's Google Play listing sets a minimum of Android 5.0 and shows Phone and Tablet device chips. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12, the A10 Android 14 and the A6 Android 15, all with Google Play, so each meets the published minimum. Clik publishes no RAM, storage or screen requirement. The app's last update was 8 July 2024, so install it on one device and run a job before buying a fleet; we have not tested it ourselves.

Clik Service is Windows office software and its one published requirement is .NET Framework 4.7.2 or higher on a PC with current Windows updates, which a Windows 11 Pro device such as the W10 carries. Clik does not publish processor, RAM or disk figures for Clik Service, so for a large database ask Clik's support team before relying on an Intel N100 with 8GB. The W10 cannot run the Clik Jobs app, which is Android and iOS only.

Yes, according to Clik: the Google Play listing says the app is designed to function almost completely without an active internet connection and only needs one to sync, and the support centre FAQ says engineers can download jobs before going to site and sync them back later. Jobs reach the device only when Clik Service runs a sync, so a scheduled sync and a connection in the van matter. The Tuga A8, A10 and A6 all have dual SIM 4G for that.

That is a question for Clik or Joblogic, not for us.
